title: bug: middleware does not rewrite requests to the target endpoint
description:
There appears to be a problem in the tableau extension. I can see that if I make a request to Connect (as if the request is coming from tableau by setting the user agent)

```
❯ curl -v -X 'POST' -u rstudio-connect:$CONNECT_INSECURE_DEFAULT_API_KEY \
  'http://localhost:3939/evaluate' \
  -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'user-agent: tableau' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "script": "/content/ff1d687c-e645-4668-822e-228cb9cd096f/capitalize",
  "data": {
    "_arg1": [
      "mystring that should be capitalized"
    ]
  }
}'
Note: Unnecessary use of -X or --request, POST is already inferred.

<

{"message":"Server Error: HTTPException","info":"Not Found"}
```
 
Then we get a 404. However, I can also see that the request is being routed to the content correctly, even when connect is running behind a proxy subpath:
 
```
time="2026-02-10T17:08:18.168Z" level=debug msg="Request contentRoute = /content/ff1d687c-e645-4668-822e-228cb9cd096f, original targetPath = /content/ff1d687c-e645-4668-822e-228cb9cd096f/capitalize, adjusted targetPath = /capitalize" correlation_id=0a1e4044-1360-49b6-ac30-839b8e0cc30c region=tableau-integration
time="2026-02-10T17:08:18.168Z" level=debug msg="Script value in body adjusted from /content/ff1d687c-e645-4668-822e-228cb9cd096f/capitalize to /capitalize" correlation_id=0a1e4044-1360-49b6-ac30-839b8e0cc30c region=tableau-integration
time="2026-02-10T17:08:18.168Z" level=debug msg="Rewriting URL from /evaluate to /content/ff1d687c-e645-4668-822e-228cb9cd096f/evaluate" correlation_id=0a1e4044-1360-49b6-ac30-839b8e0cc30c region=tableau-integration
time="2026-02-10T17:08:18.168Z" level=debug msg="Passing request onward in filter chain for futher processing." correlation_id=0a1e4044-1360-49b6-ac30-839b8e0cc30c region=tableau-integration
time="2026-02-10T17:08:18.172Z" level=info msg=content.hit content.guid=ff1d687c-e645-4668-822e-228cb9cd096f event.name=content.hit url.path=/evaluate user.guid=10878657-a6fe-4344-92a0-147fa443ca8e user_agent.original=tableau
```
 
If I update my content to include an evaluate endpoint, then the same request succeeds:
 
```
from typing import List
from fastapitableau import FastAPITableau

app = FastAPITableau(
    title="Simple Example",
    description="A *simple* example FastAPITableau app.",
    version="0.1.0",
)

@app.post("/capitalize")
async def capitalize(text: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    capitalized = [t.upper() for t in text]
    return capitalized


@app.post("/evaluate")
async def evaluate(text: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    capitalized = [t.upper() for t in text]
    return capitalized
```

title: Feature Request:  Tableau Table Extensions
description:
I would love to see Tableau's new feature "Table Extensions" eventually be integrated into `fastapitableau`. It seems more extensive than Analytics Extensions and more powerful in terms of it being able to access the whole Tableau Data Model, perform code on it, and return it to Tableau.
https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/tc_table_extensions.htm

title: Extension path on RStudio Connect picks up proxy path
description:
If there's a proxy in front of RSC, the path provided in the Tableau User docs includes the proxy path, instead of just the path specific to RSC:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10444878/141022227-0adaf4f5-b575-4cfd-992f-fb573a0d75e0.png)

In this example, the path relative to RSC is `/james/fastapi-test/capitalize`, but `fastapitableau` is picking up on the `rsc` part of the path and including it. If a user copies and uses the suggested path, the extension will fail from Tableau:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10444878/141022749-a38871cc-3b0f-4c1b-a2cc-1ae8122def06.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10444878/141022538-e6e0a6ee-2472-4d98-a59d-517f973b7af9.png)

If the `/rsc` is removed from the path, the extension works as expected from Tableau:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10444878/141022813-72635ab1-f6e1-42e0-99f1-2334f57bf49e.png)

title: Improve the display of route-based warning messages, particularly in the user guide
description:
Right now, when type annotations are insufficient for us to generate Tableau usage examples, we [display a warning message in its place](https://github.com/rstudio/fastapitableau/blob/e4f979725edd886ed7eb25e5c9848c4a5e617c81/fastapitableau/user_guide.py#L89).

We could instead pass this data up to the RouteInfo object and use this to alter the display of the function in the user guide, to provide a more distinct and informative warning message.

This would also be a good place to surface warnings about endpoints that do not meet Tableau criteria (i.e. with too-complex Pydantic models). We could display a warning message at the top of the landing page to the effect of "Some endpoints will not work with Tableau. Click here [link to user guide] to see more." In the user guide, we could display more informative message about endpoints that won't work.

title: Add query parameters to the Tableau code snippets we generate in the Tableau Usage page
Consider enabling support for self-signed certificates in the `warning_message()` function.
description: This would be controlled via an environment variable. However, I'm not sure if it's really necessary.

title: Consider if we want to change the conditions under which we rewrite request bodies.
description: Right now, we check [here](https://github.com/rstudio/fastapitableau/blob/e4f979725edd886ed7eb25e5c9848c4a5e617c81/fastapitableau/routing.py#L41) for the presence of `script` and `data` keys. We could include a custom header, or check for Tableau headers.

title: Print more verbose log messages when a debug environment variable is present
description:
Some thoughts:

- We should log the various warning message conditions.

title: The language in warning messages needs to be reviewed
description: In addition, tests should be added to the `warning_message()` function to ensure its output under a variety of states.

title: Pydantic schemas are not supported in API definitions
description:
We need to support using Pydantic schemas in function definitions. These will still be limited to flat collections of lists, due to the limitations imposed by Tableau's data model, but we should still support them because they allow for re-use of code, and are the primary way of defining data models that FastAPI describes.

We could also use this as a chance to think about #25.
